summary: Researched current official guidance for serving a same-origin static frontend from FastAPI, consuming POST-based SSE with browser fetch streaming, and bootstrapping the existing session model safely.

findings.topic: FastAPI frontend serving and route precedence
findings.conclusion: Current FastAPI guidance recommends app.frontend('/', directory='static') for a generated static frontend. FastAPI checks normal path operations before frontend files, so existing /api routes remain authoritative. The default fallback is auto: a missing browser navigation can use index.html, while missing assets remain 404 and non-GET/HEAD fallback requests remain 404. This is preferable to a catch-all API route and is appropriate for a root static directory.

StaticFiles is a mounted ASGI application for a directory; html=True serves index.html for directory requests and returns normal 404/405 responses for misses. FileResponse is a single-file response and supplies useful file metadata such as Content-Length, Last-Modified, ETag, and range support. HTMLResponse is a direct in-memory HTML response and does not solve serving sibling CSS/JS/assets. Therefore a single FileResponse or HTMLResponse root handler would require additional asset routes and more routing logic; a directory mount or app.frontend is smaller and more robust.

findings.topic: Preserving /api routes with a root frontend
findings.conclusion: Starlette matches routes in order and documents that more specific routes must precede general routes. If app.frontend is unavailable in the installed FastAPI version, the compatibility fallback is to include the API routers first and then mount StaticFiles(directory='static', html=True) at '/'. The root mount then handles frontend files while the already-registered /api operations win. Do not mount the root static application before API routes.

The project already returns text/event-stream through StreamingResponse. Each application event is emitted as one data line containing JSON followed by a blank line; heartbeat comments are emitted as ': ping\n\n'. The browser parser must ignore colon comment records, dispatch only complete records terminated by a blank line, decode UTF-8, and parse the JSON in each data field. The standard format also permits multiple data lines and named event/id/retry fields, so a small parser should at least accumulate data lines rather than assuming every record is one physical network chunk.

findings.topic: POST SSE: fetch streaming versus EventSource
findings.conclusion: EventSource is designed around constructing a URL plus the withCredentials option; its standard interface has no request method, body, or arbitrary request-header parameters. It also reconnects automatically when a connection ends. The existing chat endpoints are POST /api/sessions/{session_id}/turns and POST /api/sessions/{session_id}/retry with JSON bodies, so EventSource cannot call them without changing the backend contract. Use fetch with method POST, Content-Type application/json, Accept text/event-stream, and a ReadableStream reader/TextDecoderStream. Check response.ok before reading because fetch resolves for HTTP error statuses, and use AbortController for user cancellation.

findings.topic: Fetch stream parsing and reconnect behavior
findings.conclusion: Fetch response bodies are ReadableStreams and can be processed incrementally with TextDecoderStream and async iteration. Network chunks are not SSE records, so retain a buffer across reads and parse line/blank-line framing. The existing endpoint emits no id fields; native Last-Event-ID resumption is therefore not available. The project already supplies client_msg_id and tests duplicate/completed turns as replayable, so retries should be explicit and deliberate rather than relying on EventSource automatic reconnection, which could duplicate a POST. Abort the fetch on stop and, if the UI needs server-side cancellation, call the existing /stop endpoint separately.

For a frontend served by the same FastAPI origin, fetch's default credentials mode is same-origin; an explicit credentials:'same-origin' is acceptable for clarity. Prefer sessionStorage for this local single-tab workflow when cross-tab persistence is not required. If resume across restarts is a requirement, localStorage may hold only an opaque, server-issued session id, but it is readable by any script running in the origin and must not contain API keys, bearer tokens, or message content. Read defensively, bound and validate the value as an opaque identifier, URL-encode it in a path, GET the session to verify it still exists, clear stale/invalid storage, and create a new session only after verification fails. Serialize bootstrap through one promise so concurrent UI initialization cannot create multiple sessions. Do not interpolate stored values into HTML; use textContent/DOM APIs.

If authentication is added later, a server-issued Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookie is safer for a session secret because frontend JavaScript cannot read HttpOnly cookies and fetch still sends them on same-origin requests. Frontend code cannot inspect Set-Cookie. This is not needed for the current repository's random database session ids, but should be preferred over exposing an authentication token to storage if an auth layer is introduced.

recommendations: Use app.frontend('/', directory='static') after all API routers are included when the installed FastAPI version supports the current frontend helper. It gives root asset serving, index fallback behavior, and documented API precedence in one call.

If the project's installed FastAPI predates app.frontend, use StaticFiles(directory='static', html=True) mounted at '/' after include_router calls. Avoid a hand-written HTMLResponse/FileResponse catch-all unless the frontend is truly one file with no sibling assets.

Implement one fetch-based POST SSE helper for turns and retries. Set the JSON request headers, check response.ok and content type, stream through TextDecoderStream, buffer across chunks, ignore heartbeat comments, accumulate data lines, JSON.parse each complete event, and expose AbortController cancellation.
Do not use EventSource for the existing POST endpoints. Keep reconnection/retry explicit and keyed by the existing client_msg_id to avoid silently repeating a state-changing request.

Bootstrap the active session from sessionStorage by default: read one bounded opaque id, verify it with GET /api/sessions/{id}, remove it on a 404 or invalid value, and POST /api/sessions only when no valid session remains. Keep the bootstrap promise singleton and never store secrets or render the id as HTML.

Add focused integration coverage for GET / returning index.html, asset retrieval, an API route still resolving under the root frontend, chunk-boundary SSE parsing including ': ping', non-2xx fetch handling, abort behavior, stale session recovery, and duplicate-bootstrap prevention.
notes: The repository currently defines API routers under /api, chat streaming as POST endpoints backed by StreamingResponse, and server-generated random hexadecimal ids via new_id(). requirements.txt leaves FastAPI unpinned, so verify app.frontend exists in the deployed environment; StaticFiles is the conservative compatibility fallback. No source files were modified.
